Title.rationale: `public override string Title` appends `+{FakeUpgradeLevel}` to the card name (Wither.cs:16-27) so a fake-upgraded Wither reads "Wither+2". Presentation -- the sim has no card-title layer -- but worth recording because it is the only `Title` override in the pool and it exists precisely because FakeUpgrade does not touch `CurrentUpgradeLevel`.

MaxUpgradeLevel.rationale: `=> 0` (Wither.cs:42) == the class attribute, and it is what forces the fake-upgrade mechanism to exist: Wither can never be really upgraded, so Aeonglass grows it through a side channel.

CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ CardKeyword.Unplayable }` (Wither.cs:46) == `is_playable = False`. No Ethereal and no Exhaust, so Wither stays in hand and keeps hurting every turn.

ctor.issue: STATUS / STATUS / NONE map exactly. The canonical energy cost is -1 in C# and 0 in the sim. `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), so the game's unplayable card is immune to every cost modifier; the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain (cards/base.py:222-232). Only what is READ diverges. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/ascenders_bane's ctor entry (rule 3). DORMANT: every ported cost reader filters `> 0` or skips `<= 1`, and events/infested_automaton.py:35 filters pool_card_ids(), which holds no curses or statuses.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: the base 3 lives in the `_BASE_DAMAGE` class constant and a `damage` property (wither.py:157, 163-165)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new DamageVar(3m, ValueProp.Unpowered | ValueProp.Move)` (Wither.cs:44) is the printed damage, and the SIM'S ARITHMETIC IS RIGHT: C# grows it by mutating the var (`DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(3m)` inside `FakeUpgrade`, Wither.cs:65) while the sim recomputes it as `_BASE_DAMAGE + _BASE_DAMAGE * fake_upgrade_level` (3, 6, 9, ...), which is the same sequence -- and the sim's form is strictly better behaved, because `fake_upgrade_level` is re-seeded in `_init_vars` so a downgrade cannot corrupt it (contrast card/maul, card/rampage and card/thrash, which mutate their damage in place and lose it). What is missing is only the STORAGE SHAPE: there is no `_damage` attribute, so `Card.base_damage` (cards/base.py:191-195) returns None and the observation encoder sees no damage for Wither even though `damage` is right at the use site. The PROP SET is reproduced correctly: the sim passes no explicit props and `DamageCmd.deal` infers `DamageProps.CARD_UNPOWERED` (UNPOWERED | MOVE) from `is_unpowered = True` (cmds.py:44-50, wither.py:154), so the damage is not Strength-scaled and IS blockable on both sides -- identical to card/burn, card/decay, card/infection and card/toxic. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed number the sim's printed-number API cannot surface, so `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card without it. DORMANT for game fidelity, LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnTurnEndInHand.rationale: `CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.Damage, this)` (Wither.cs:59) -- passing the VAR so the props ride along -- == `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, self.damage, dealer=None, card=self)`. Explicit null dealer on both sides, and the amount is the fake-upgraded value on both.

OnPlay.rationale: Wither.cs declares no OnPlay and the card is Unplayable.

guards.what: FakeUpgrade is a plain public method, not an override, so the harness does not enumerate it (Wither.cs:62-66)
guards.rationale: `FakeUpgradeLevel++` plus `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(3m)` == the sim's `fake_upgrade()` incrementing `fake_upgrade_level` (wither.py:167-169), with the damage following from the property. The Aeonglass boss's "Increasing Intensity" move is the caller and belongs to the monster stream; the sim's docstring records that it fake-upgrades every existing Wither and matches newly generated ones to its count.
